blocking: Cultural descriptions sometimes prescribe a family's sequence despite promising to follow its customs.
Language support sounds guaranteed across six languages; the qualification is buried on the services page.
Several 'Call or WhatsApp' links open only WhatsApp, frustrating parents who expect a telephone call.

fixes.what: Replace categorical phrases such as 'the sangeet is its own night', 'elders’ blessing first' and 'Seven circuits under the mandap' with family-confirmed descriptions. Remove the rigid distinction 'the reception is the couple’s'. Apply the family-choice qualification within each relevant description.
fixes.why: Specificity builds trust only when it leaves room for the family's actual practice.

fixes.where: Shared footer; index.html #journey; how-we-work.html language FAQ
fixes.what: Use 'Tell us your family’s preferred language; written translations and spoken support are confirmed in your proposal' consistently beside language promises.
fixes.why: Parents need to distinguish translated documents from a planner who can speak with them directly.

fixes.what: Split 'Call or WhatsApp' into 'Call (925) 263-9949' linked to tel:+19252639949 and a separate WhatsApp link.
fixes.why: The promised calling route should work without requiring WhatsApp.

fixes.what: Put the actual booking requirements and date-reservation point directly after Proposal; clarify whether an inquiry or consultation holds availability.
fixes.why: Families coordinating several dates need to know exactly when their planner is secured.

fixes.what: Add a concise operational explanation of how simultaneous events, venue changes, delays and planner absence are handled, with staffing and backup arrangements confirmed in the proposal.
fixes.why: Multi-day competence needs evidence beyond repeated promises of one timeline and one contact.

fixes.what: Keep celebration names horizontal and immediately scannable, using a compact selector above the expanded panel instead of rotated labels.
fixes.why: Parents should recognize their ceremony without rotating their head or exploring each narrow strip.
